REFERENCE
What is ERA Standardization?

Optum generates 835 (ERA) remittance files with standard X12 delimiters — a segment terminator (~) and an element separator (*) — usually delivered as one continuous line of text.

The problem

Providers read ERAs in different systems — EHRs, RCM tools, or by hand. One continuous line is hard to read and debug, causes parsing mismatches when a system expects another format, and slows reconciliation.

How it helps

You can change the segment terminator and element separator within controlled limits, so the file is reshaped for human reading without touching the data underneath.

  • Easier reading and debugging of remittance files
  • Faster reconciliation against your practice management system
  • No change to the underlying claim or payment data
  • Full X12 compatibility — only a controlled, limited set of characters can change

CARC and RARC consolidation

Claim adjustment codes are normalized so your practice management system sees consistent, predictable values.

Always locked
Never remapped, in any configuration.
CARC 1 2 3 — patient responsibility
CARC 45 94 — financial and contractual integrity
CARC 16 · RARC N30 — the anchors themselves
Conditionally locked
Remappable only when explicitly allowed; locked by default.
CARC 29 — timely filing
CARC 119 — benefit max
RARC N20 — not covered
Everything else
Consolidates onto the two anchors.
Other CARCs → CAS*CO*16
Other RARCs → LQ*HE*N30

Source: Priyanka’s 835 standardization requirements. Per-payer ID replacement is out of scope for 2.0.
